title: Vertex vs Dirichlet proxy-mix design for linear domain attribution
setting: A synthetic oracle maps a data mix over d domains (capped simplex with uniform caps 1/K) to a performance score in [0,1] through a sparse hidden linear attribution, an optional random pairwise-interaction term and a sigmoid. A budget of 4d noisy proxy evaluations is spent on a design (random capped-simplex vertices, or Dirichlet mixes around a skewed prior), a surrogate is fit (OLS or gradient boosting), and the selected mix is scored on the noise-free oracle. The metric is regret against a local-search near-optimal mix.

paper.title: LinMix: Data Mixing as Linear Domain Attribution
paper.claim: Sampling proxy mixes at capped-simplex vertices supports a reliable linear fit and better mix selection than Dirichlet sampling (even with a nonlinear surrogate), especially with many domains and when Dirichlet mixes concentrate near the prior.

metric.name: true_regret
metric.description: Noise-free oracle score of a near-optimal reference mix minus the oracle score of the mix selected by the method (clipped at 0). Lower is better. Diagnostics: sign_agree, coef_corr, chosen_perf, ref_perf.

factors.name: method
factors.description: dirichlet_gbm: Dirichlet-sampled mixes, gradient-boosting surrogate, top-10 average over a 3000-candidate Dirichlet pool (RegMix-style). linmix: paired greedy-fill vertex design with OLS and top-K cap-saturating LP solution. dirichlet_ols: Dirichlet design with OLS and the same LP solution.

factors.name: n_domains
factors.description: Number of domains d; proxy budget is 4d runs and K=round(d/4) domains fit in the budget.

factors.name: nonlinearity
factors.description: Weight of the random pairwise-interaction term in the oracle (0 = linear before the sigmoid).

factors.name: concentration
factors.description: Per-domain Dirichlet concentration (total = value*d, log-uniform jitter): 0.3 gives sparse spread-out mixes, 30 gives mixes tightly concentrated near the prior. Ignored by linmix.
